results.evidence: I did not run the exact AC command through the CLI. The AC's own scenario is the test test_call_with_stage_moves_lead_and_records_stage_change in tests/test_events_stages.py, which has the same shape with the pinned clock. It sets up inbound lead 1 at candidate, runs log-event 1 call --at AT --stage contacted_or_replied, and asserts exit 0 and leads.stage == contacted_or_replied. It also asserts that the activities are exactly [call, stage_change], that both have the same occurred_at, and that the stage_change payload is {from: candidate, to: contacted_or_replied, event_activity_id: call id}. Its last assertion is that stdout contains 'stage candidate -> contacted_or_replied'. The full file passes (34 passed). In cottonwood/events.py, log_event inserts the event, updates leads.stage, and inserts one stage_change with the same occurred_at in one transaction. cottonwood/cli.py appends '; stage {from} -> {to}' to the output line.

events.py defines DIRECT_STAGES (9 values) and RELATIONSHIP_STAGES (6 values), both matching R-14 exactly. STAGES_BY_LEAD_TYPE maps inbound_inquiry and direct_candidate to DIRECT_STAGES and relationship_prospect to RELATIONSHIP_STAGES. _check_stage refuses only a stage outside the lead type's list or equal to the current stage, so there is no ordering constraint. The tests run each non-current stage through the CLI for the matching lead types: test_every_direct_stage_is_accepted for lead 1 and lead 2, and test_every_relationship_stage_is_accepted for lead 3. _move passes --need when the stage is buyer_need_confirmed. test_moves_in_any_order covers non-sequential moves (won -> researched -> closed_no_fit -> candidate -> buyer_need_confirmed). All 49 tests in test_events_stages.py and test_events_qualify.py passed.

refutation upheld: cottonwood/events.py:142-154: validate_event runs the R-16 checks before log_event reaches _check_stage at events.py:180. So `--stage buyer_need_confirmed` with no --need on a relationship_prospect lead (outside that type's list) is refused with 'buyer_need_confirmed needs --need ...'. A bogus stage given with --need is refused with 'only allowed with --stage buyer_need_confirmed'. Neither message lists the type's allowed stages, which AC3 requires. (refuter: I read the code and did not run a CLI probe. validate_event() runs before log_event()/_check_stage(), so it can reject an out-of-list stage with a message that does not list the allowed stages. Example: a relationship_prospect lead with `--stage buyer_need_confirmed` and no --need or --procurement-url. buyer_need_confirmed is only in DIRECT_STAGES, so it is outside that type's list. validate_event raises 'buyer_need_confirmed needs --need ...' and never reaches _check_stage. Likewise, a bogus or out-of-list stage given with --need or --procurement-url is rejected with 'only allowed with --stage buyer_need_confirmed'. In both cases stderr does not list the type's allowed stages, which the AC requires. The stage-list message exists only in _check_stage, reached only after validate_event passes. The 34 tests in tests/test_events_stages.py pass, but they do not cover these paths.)

I ran tests/test_events_qualify.py and all 15 tests passed. test_need_qualifies_and_is_stored calls the CLI with --stage buyer_need_confirmed --need 'needs 4,000 sq ft office TI by March'. It asserts exit 0, that the stage is buyer_need_confirmed, and that the event payload's need equals that text. test_procurement_url_qualifies_and_is_stored does the same with --procurement-url https://bids.example.gov/rfp/123 and asserts exit 0 and payload['procurement_url'] equals the URL. events.py:207-210 writes need and procurement_url into the activity payload. cli.py adds the --stage, --need and --procurement-url arguments and passes them to RawEvent. I did not run the CLI by hand outside the test suite.

validate_event in cottonwood/events.py refuses buyer_need_confirmed when need and procurement_url are both empty after _clean. That covers a missing or whitespace-only --need. It also refuses a procurement URL that is not absolute http(s) with a host, which covers 'bids.example.gov/rfp' and 'ftp://x/y'. It refuses --need or --procurement-url whenever the stage is not buyer_need_confirmed, which covers no --stage and --stage walkthrough. These checks run before any DB write. cli.py maps EventError to EXIT_REFUSED (1). tests/test_events_qualify.py parametrizes these cases. Each asserts exit 1, an 'error:' message on stderr, an unchanged activity count and the stage still 'candidate'. All 15 tests passed. I did not run the CLI by hand, and I did not read the whitespace-only --need parametrization. I read only part of the file, and the cited line 150 is the no-stage/walkthrough refusal branch.

It then runs log-event with --stage researched. It asserts the exit code is EXIT_REFUSED (1 at cli.py:18), stderr starts with 'error:' and has no 'Traceback', the activity count is unchanged, and the lead's stage is still 'candidate'. cli.py:324-326 catches sqlite3.Error, prints 'error: could not save the event: ...' and returns EXIT_REFUSED. events.log_event rolls back on any exception (`except BaseException: conn.rollback()`). A second test checks the rollback on the same connection. All 34 tests in the file pass.

The parametrized test test_disallowed_or_current_stage_is_refused (tests/test_events_stages.py:170-200) covers introduced and active_relationship on direct/inbound leads, walkthrough on a relationship prospect, bogus on both lead families, and the current stage on both. It asserts exit 1, stderr starting with 'error:' and listing every allowed stage, an unchanged activity count and an unchanged stage. All 54 tests in the two new test files pass. One gap: I did not confirm that lead 2 in the test fixture is the inbound lead. Both lead types share DIRECT_STAGES, so the logic is the same either way.
